urls.description: Abstract. Engineered T-cell therapies are limited by progressive dysfunction under chronic tumor antigen exposure, and genetic perturbation of negative regulators has emerged as a promising strategy to sustain effector activity. We reanalyzed a genome-wide CRISPR knockout screen in primary human T cells under repetitive tumor stimulation; protein–protein interaction mapping revealed seven members of the Cullin–RING Ligase 5 (CRL5) complex as an enriched hit cluster. Knockout of any of these members (CUL5, ARIH2, RNF7, UBE2F, UBE2L3, CISH, DCUN1D3) enhanced tumor serial killing, and CUL5, the complex scaffold, emerged as the strongest target. CUL5 knockout T cells exhibited sustained cytotoxicity, elevated effector cytokine production, and fewer exhaustion marker–positive cells while retaining antigen specificity and cytokine dependence.
